local_changes.scope: Private native ZML source experiment; upstream f430c353 does not load this split-expert checkpoint.
local_changes.model: Native AWQ INT4/asymmetric, group size 128; BF16 weights in layer 0, AWQ weights in 39 layers; decode dequantizes only the eight selected experts.
local_changes.chat: The local CLI implements the checkpoint chat template with thinking disabled and recognizes both generation EOS IDs.
local_changes.build: Bazel CUDA backend. Sequential compilation, 128 MiB loader DMA pool.

fused_awq_decode.implementation: Second local ZML build using fused dequantization and FP32 projection for eight selected experts during single-token decode.
fused_awq_decode.projection_oracle: Eight BF16 results on a tile of real checkpoint weights matched an independent CPU calculation exactly (absolute tolerance zero). Changing the FP32 reduction order can affect subsequent tokens.

fused_awq_prefill.implementation: Fourth local build. The routed Triton prefill kernel unpacks and scales each expert tile as needed; the eight-step GDN recurrence and single-token decode path are shared with the preceding build.

full_layer.input: Real checkpoint embeddings and router weights applied to the common Lyon prompt. This isolates a layer using surrogate hidden states.
full_layer.timing: One warmup per implementation, followed by seven synchronous calls. Weight loading and graph compilation occur before timing.

prefill_profile.request: A second, independently profiled Lyon request with the same 227 input IDs and 64 output IDs as the timed Lyon request.
prefill_profile.durations: Each family sums kernel durations, which can overlap. Wall time covers the instrumented prefill.

grouped_awq_decode.implementation: Fifth local build, with one-token AWQ expert projections grouped by quantization block, routed expert and output tile. Float32 partial sums are reduced before the BF16 cast.

layer_oracle.description: Real checkpoint embeddings used as surrogate layer inputs. The router and all eight selected experts use the real layer weights. Independent CPU AWQ unpacking uses FP64 reductions and explicit BF16 intermediate rounding.

weight_rounding_check.optimized_xla: Both projections enter XLA with explicit FP16 to BF16 to FP32 conversion; optimized HLO converts packed-weight products directly from FP16 to FP32 before the reduction.
